data.text: High-fidelity audio technologies clearly improve the immersive experience in VR. Augmenting vision with audio enhances immersion because vision alone may not give a full picture. Combining sound with vision reinforces the perception of properties like size and distance, making virtual experiences believable and helping to create an emotional connection. The auditory experience plays a very important role in increasing presence by reinforcing believability and attachment.
points: High-fidelity audio technologies clearly improve the immersive experience in VR.
Augmenting vision with audio enhances immersion because vision alone may not give a full picture.
Combining sound with vision reinforces the perception of properties like size, volume, and distance.
Audio makes a virtual experience believable and helps create an emotional connection.
Audio plays a very important role in increasing presence by reinforcing believability and attachment.

data.text: Sound is a vibration in a medium, usually air, but it requires a medium to propagate. Pressure variations are converted by the human eardrum into auditory experiences and can be represented as sound waves plotted against time. These waves are primarily characterized by frequency, amplitude, phase, and the human audible frequency range.
points: Sound is a vibration in a medium, usually air, but it requires a medium to propagate.
Pressure variations in a medium are converted by the human eardrum into auditory experiences.
Sound waves are plots of pressure variation against time.
Sound waves are primarily characterized by frequency, amplitude, phase, and the human audible frequency range.

data.text: The human hearing system consists of the outer, middle, and inner ear. The outer ear receives and amplifies sound while attenuating high-frequency waves, which then strike the tympanic membrane in the middle ear to transfer vibrations to three ossicles. Finally, the inner ear's cochlea converts this sound energy into neural impulses that are transmitted to the brain.
points: The human hearing system contains the outer, middle, and inner ear.
The outer ear receives and amplifies sound while attenuating high-frequency sound waves.
The middle ear vibrates the tympanic membrane to transfer vibrations to three ossicles.
The inner ear's cochlea converts sound energy into neural impulses for the brain.
